items.name: Mannfield
items.description: Mannfield is an arena in Rocket League. It is one of the two venues where the Championship match can be played in Season mode. Mannfield has a stormy variation. A night variation was added on March 22, 2017, as part of the Dropshot update. A snowy variant of the arena was added on September 28, 2017 as part of the Autumn Update.

items.name: Urban Central
items.description: Urban Central is an arena in Rocket League, based on the SARPBC (Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle Cars) arena Urban. Urban Central has a night variation, which was added on October 13, 2015, along with the release of the Revenge of the Battle-Cars DLC pack; and a dawn variation, which was added on September 8, 2016, along with the release of Rumble. Unlike other arenas, Urban Central have specific stingers during epic saves, but are retired as of Patch v1.43.

items.name: Neo Tokyo
items.description: The Neo Tokyo arena was added to Rocket League on May 10, 2017. Comic version was added with Season 6 in Patch v2.12. It is based on the previous version of Neo Tokyo, Tokyo Underpass, which was removed from online playlists on March 22, 2017.

items.name: Farmstead
items.description: Farmstead is an arena released on September 28, 2017, as part of the Autumn Update. By the launch of Season 13, a fourth variant, Farmstead (Pitched) was added.

items.name: Rivals Arena
items.description: The Rivals Arena is an arena which was added to Rocket League on September 24, 2018, in partnership with Hot Wheels. This arena is based on the Champions Field arena, but with a different background, different banners and the Hot Wheels logo replacing the Psyonix logo on the jumbotron screens. The Rivals Arena is available in exhibition matches, private matches and tournament modes. It is not included in online playlists.

items.name: Salty Shores
items.description: Salty Shores is an arena that was released on May 29, 2018. The surrounding beach seems to be inspired by Venice Beach, California. An almost identical pier to the Santa Monica Pier can be seen, and the Hollywood sign (which is displayed as 'Hagewood') can also be seen.

items.name: Beckwith Park
items.description: Beckwith Park is an arena in Rocket League, named after Rocket League Level Designer and Psyonix Technical Artist, Ben Beckwith. It is also where all Training game modes take place. Beckwith Park has stormy and midnight variations.

items.name: Neon Fields
items.description: Neon Fields is an arena in Rocket League. It was added to the game on December 9 2020, it comes as part of Season 2. If a player does not have equipped a player anthem if he scores a goal, the instrumental version of Flip Reset is heard. However, if a player has equipped the Flip Reset player anthem, the vocal version is heard.

items.name: Duel (1v1)
items.description: Duel previously known as Solo Duel is arguably the most balanced in terms of raw skill. Because it is simply a one-on-one game, solo duel is not based at all on co-operating in a team, but on strategy and skill in the arena.

items.name: Doubles (2v2)
items.description: Doubles is a popular competitive playlist. Doubles is very popular because standard tends to balance the game less proportionally when there are more players to play with or against. In doubles, you need to co-operate with only one teammate.

items.name: Standard (3v3)
items.description: Standard is generally the most popular competitive playlist. As the name indicates, it is the standard online game mode. In standard, the team is composed of three players, therefore, teamwork is crucial to victory. Because of the number of players involved in the gameplay, it is recommended that players maintain tactical positions and rotation across the arena.

items.name: Chaos (4v4)
items.description: Chaos is a Casual playlist for bigger parties, you can bring a team of 4 to the game of 4v4 on standard arenas.

items.name: Rumble
items.description: Rumble is an epic battle royale-style addition which was released on September 8th 2016 and comes stacked with randomized power-ups. Whether you’re equipped with the Haymaker, the Swapper, or the Tornado, each one of the 11 new power-ups brings an extra dimension to the classic Rocket League formula.

items.name: Dropshot
items.description: Dropshot is a brand new take on Rocket League gameplay as we introduce dynamic breakable floors and an electrified ball, all within the confines of a new hexagonal Arena, Core 707. Instead of pushing the ball into your opponent's goal, your objective is to destroy panels on the opposing team's floor, and score goals through those gaps.

items.name: Snow Day
items.description: Snow Day is a game mode in Rocket League where the ball is replaced by a hockey puck. It is currently available in Online Playlists, Private matches and Exhibition matches.

items.name: Hoops
items.description: Hoops is a basketball-style game mode added on April 25, 2016, in which the goals are replaced by two baskets. It is the only mode that uses the Dunk House arena. Hoops is available to play in the Extra Modes playlist and in offline games.

items.name: Octane
items.description: The Octane is a vehicle body released on July 7, 2015, along with the game release. It originally appeared in the Rocket League precursor Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars. The Octane is classified as Base rarity. The Octane is one of the three bodies that can be unlocked at the beginning of the game. It has remained the most popular body in the game since Rocket League's release. It is by far the most popular with high ranked players and the most used by champion players during the Rocket League Championship Series.

items.name: Dominus
items.description: The Dominus is a vehicle released on August 13, 2015, which could only be obtained as DLC from the Supersonic Fury DLC Pack before it was made unlockable for free without purchase. The Dominus hitbox, used by other cars, is based off of it. It has remained the most popular premium body in the game since the first DLC's release as it is one of the most popular by high ranked players. It resembles a 1969 Pontiac GTO.

items.name: Fennec
items.description: Fennec is a vehicle body that was released on July 1, 2019, which could originally be obtained from the Totally Awesome Crate. As of today, since Crates are retired, it can be obtained from Blueprints, Trade-ins or from Item Shop. Before December 5 2023, it could also be obtained through trading between players. This car is among the most popular by high ranked players. Due to its popularity, on February 1, 2021, Fennec versions of the Esports Shop decals were released for all available teams.

items.name: Scarab
items.description: Scarab is a battle-car released on October 13, 2015, which could be obtained from the Revenge of the Battle-Cars DLC pack. It originally appeared in the Rocket League precursor, Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars.

items.name: Merc
items.description: Merc is a vehicle body released on July 7, 2015, with the release of the game. It is one of the three bodies already unlocked at the beginning of the game since Free To Play. It is classified as Common rarity.

items.name: Nissan Skyline
items.description: The Fast & Furious Nissan Skyline was originally released as '99 Nissan Skyline GT-R R34. '99 Nissan Skyline GT-R R34 is a battle-car released as licensed DLC on October 11, 2017. It was retired in December of 2019, but it made a return in the Fast & Furious Bundle and also in its own Single Car Bundle F&F Nissan Skyline Bundle and was available from June 17, 2021 to June 30, 2021.

items.name: Batmobile
items.description: The Batmobile is a battle-car released on March 8, 2016, which could only be obtained from the Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice DLC pack. It is not compatible with most decals, wheels, rocket boosts, trails, or anything else other than the items in the DLC pack that go with it. It can only have its paint color and goal explosion changed freely. Although not as popular as other Battle-Cars used in the Rocket League Championship Series, it has been favored by some pro-level players.

items.name: Lamborghini Huracan
items.description: The Lamborghini Huracán STO is a licensed DLC vehicle that was on sale as a bundle in the Item Shop for 2000 Credits from 04-21-2021 till 04-27-2021. The bundle includes the Lamborghini Huracán STO decal, Lamborghini Huracán STO v1 and Lamborghini Huracán STO v2 wheels, Lamborghini Huracán STO engine audio, and Lamborghini Huracán STO player banner. These items are only compatible with the Lamborghini Huracán.
